business_problem: Nantong High-Tech Holding Group needed a trusted way to circulate design, image, and production data across the home-textile ecosystem so companies could reduce duplicated material spend, protect IP, and attach AI services to shared industry data.
solution_summary: Nantong High-Tech Holding Group worked with Huawei Cloud Stack to build a trusted data space for the home-textile industry and pair it with AI innovation scenarios. The architecture follows a '1+6+N' design. The shared data-circulation infrastructure combines MRS, DWS, and DataArts Studio for data processing and product development, then adds EDS data-use control, TICS privacy computing, and BCS blockchain evidence and audit for trusted circulation. A six-party trust framework coordinates platform operators, data providers, demanders, service providers, and supervisory roles. On top of that governed base, the group landed services such as a high-quality image library, IP protection, industry benchmarks, smart quality inspection, and a smart logistics network. The solution turns dispersed design and production data into controllable, auditable data products and feeds AI-enabled applications that help manufacturers reduce design waste, inspect defects, and coordinate the textile chain.
products_used: EDS, TICS, and BCS trusted-circulation services

data_flow: Design assets, images, and other home-textile data are ingested into the trusted data-space infrastructure, processed through MRS, DWS, and DataArts Studio, and then circulated under EDS, TICS, and BCS controls. Those governed datasets are used by the home-textile large model and downstream services such as image libraries, quality inspection, and logistics applications.

business_outcome: The trusted data space activated data sharing across the local home-textile cluster and produced measurable gains in design speed, cost control, and defect detection for participating enterprises.
